title: Singapore Manufacturing Logistics Control Tower
thesis: Snowflake turns daily site data from Kestrel Strait Industries, a fictional Singapore-based precision manufacturer, into on-time shipment KPIs, 7-day disruption-risk scores, shipment dwell-time anomalies and grounded AI answers. Its outbound network of factory dispatch docks, distribution centers, cross-docks, container yards and port terminals spans Tuas, Pasir Panjang, Jurong East, Woodlands, Changi and Seletar, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: On-time shipments, supply disruptions, exception moves and shipments handled for 30 sites across 6 Singapore planning areas.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to site-day rows and the shipments behind them.
The late-shipments chart shows which disruption causes push the most shipments past their committed delivery window.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of island-wide logistics KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which sites are likely to cause the next disruption?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each site's probability of a supply disruption in the next 7 days.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent labelled days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags shipment dwell-time outliers per site, and the forecast projects network-wide shipment volume for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: How healthy are the sites behind those risks?

talking_points: Equipment uptime and equipment readiness (forklifts, reach trucks, quay cranes, dock doors and reach stackers) frame the response capacity.
PM compliance against on-time shipments by site shows where maintenance discipline and delivery performance move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised actions from the KPI, disruption, cause and risk tables only.
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when a site raises a dwell-time alarm right now?

talking_points: Live site tracker readings (shipment dwell hours, handling equipment load) land in RAW.LIVE_TELEMETRY, from the simulator or from AWS IoT Core through Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs ALARM readings with an SOP hint and the site's current risk band, then emails the shift lead.
tabs.call_out: From alarm to action in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over synthetic site SOPs.
Ask for the on-time rate by planning area, or which Pasir Panjang sites are high risk; each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (IoT Core, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
